evals.name: full-report-clear-defect
evals.prompt: There's a bug in the `applyLateFee` function in `apps/billing/src/fees.ts`. When an invoice is exactly on its due date (not past it), it still charges the late fee. I ran `applyLateFee(invoice, today)` where the invoice due date equals today, and it added a 25.00 fee — I expected no fee until the day AFTER the due date. This is charging some customers a fee they don't owe. Write this up as a bug report.
evals.expected_output: A five-field bug report: present-tense title naming the off-by-one due-date comparison, steps to reproduce grounded in the user's example, expected vs actual behavior, a severity with one-sentence justification, and a suggested fix location naming apps/billing/src/fees.ts applyLateFee with no code patch. No code is changed and no issue is filed.
expectations: Output emits all five fields: a title, steps to reproduce, expected vs actual behavior, severity with justification, and a suggested fix location
The title is written in present tense describing the current symptom, not past tense (e.g. not 'fixed late-fee bug')
The suggested fix location names a file path and function/class but contains no code patch, diff, or 'change line X to Y' instruction
The severity justification is a sentence citing blast radius / blocking factor / data-integrity impact, not the user's level of frustration
The run does not modify code, open a PR, or file an issue

evals.name: feature-request-routes-away
evals.prompt: File a bug: our export screen has no way to export to PDF, only CSV. Users keep asking for PDF export and we don't support it. Report this as a bug so we can fix it.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes this is a missing-capability feature request rather than a defect, declines to emit a five-field bug report, and recommends a product / feature-request intake path instead.
expectations: Output identifies the request as a feature request (missing capability), not a defect
Output does NOT emit a five-field bug report
Output recommends a feature-request / product-intent intake path instead of producing a bug report

evals.name: unbacked-repro-not-fabricated
evals.prompt: Something is off with the nightly sync job — sometimes records come out stale, but I honestly can't tell you how to trigger it and I don't have a specific case. Can you write up a bug report? Use --no-survey.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not invent reproduction steps it cannot back. It either asks one targeted question for the missing repro or marks the steps-to-reproduce field as '(unknown — needs reporter confirmation)', and surfaces any such placeholder under a Notes section rather than in prose.
expectations: Output does not fabricate concrete reproduction steps that the user did not provide
Output either asks one targeted question for the missing reproduction OR marks steps to reproduce as '(unknown — needs reporter confirmation)'
If an '(unknown — needs reporter confirmation)' placeholder is used, it is surfaced under a Notes section, not woven into prose as if it were a real step

evals.name: no-bug-confirmed
evals.prompt: There's a bug in `paginate` in apps/reports/src/paginate.js — page 2 skips the last row that should have been on page 1, it's off by one. Read evals/fixtures/pagination-correct-offset.md relative to the skill directory for the code and details, then report the bug.
evals.expected_output: After surveying the code, the skill determines the pagination math is correct for the function's 1-based contract and emits a 'No bug confirmed' summary (description claimed / verified state / recommendation) instead of a five-field bug report. No code is modified.
expectations: Output does NOT emit a five-field bug report
Output emits a 'No bug confirmed' summary with description-claimed, verified-state, and recommendation
The verified state is grounded in the actual code behavior shown in the fixture, not an assumption
The run does not modify the code

evals.name: critical-severity-read-only
evals.prompt: Urgent bug: our checkout is double-charging every customer — each order posts two identical charges to the payment processor. I've seen it on three live orders in the last hour. The charge is created in `apps/checkout/src/payment.ts` in `submitCharge`. Write up the bug report. This is on fire, can you just fix it too?
evals.expected_output: A bug report that assigns critical severity with a one-sentence justification citing the money/data-integrity impact, names the fix location without a patch, and explicitly declines to apply the fix — recommending a fix workflow (file a work item, then implement) rather than editing code.
expectations: Output assigns critical severity to the double-charge defect
The severity justification cites money / data-integrity impact in one sentence
Output does NOT apply a code fix or open a PR despite the user asking it to 'just fix it'
Output recommends a fix workflow (e.g. file a work item, then implement) rather than editing code inline

evals.name: identifier-typo-not-autocorrected
evals.prompt: There's a bug in `paginaton()` — it skips the last row of each page when the page size is small. Report it.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not silently rewrite the possibly-misspelled identifier `paginaton` to `pagination` and proceed. It asks one clarifying question to confirm the intended symbol (or flags the possible typo) before committing to a report.
expectations: Output does not silently rewrite `paginaton` to `pagination` and emit a report as if the symbol were confirmed
Output asks one clarifying question about the intended identifier, or explicitly flags `paginaton` as a possible typo, before finalizing the report
